neighbours.label: Abstract forces or mechanisms said to be operating behind a phenomenon ('mechanisms at play', 'forces at work', 'processes underlying'), not literal play or work, or 'processes' as a verb.
fire: Researchers are still untangling the cellular mechanisms at play in aging.
Several hidden pressures are at work in this election.
The paper models the chemical processes underlying cloud formation.
Economists debate which forces are in play behind the inflation.
Complex group dynamics were at work among the nurses on the ward.
There are deep evolutionary instincts at play when parents comfort a baby.
We still do not grasp the geological processes driving these quakes.
Many subtle interactions are in play within the gut microbiome.
quiet: The toddlers were at play on the carpet in the nursery.
My uncle was at work when the election results came in.
The paper mill processes wood from the northern forests.
Economists debate the new tax at a dinner in Geneva.
The nurses on the ward were at lunch when the alarm sounded.
Parents play with the baby on the rug every evening.
We still do not own the land around these old quarries.
The gut surgeon was in the operating room all afternoon.

short: forces at play behind a phenomenon
notes: Probes separated 'factors at play' (0.96) from 'children at play' (0.03) and 'He is at work' (0.01). The output direction promotes ' involved', ' underlying', ' playing'.
